checkpoint.contextAtWrite: wugs-s9 fully closed out this session, including a same-session fix for a bookkeeping gap: the wugs-s9-plan.md implementation-plan artefact had been written to the worktree at branch-setup time but never committed anywhere (not in any of the 4 task commits, which only staged src/test files) -- caught while assembling the DoD commit, copied from the worktree into the main checkout, and committed alongside the DoD itself. Also caught mid-DoD-write that `node bin/skills gate-advance` does NOT automatically set the `stage` field to the gate name -- it only validates the artefact against the gate and applies whatever field=value pairs are passed explicitly. Had to follow up with an explicit `stage=definition-of-done dodStatus=complete dodArtefact=...` advance call, then a direct Edit for the `tasks` array (nested arrays still need direct Edit per established practice, dot-notation advance can't reach them).
checkpoint.resumeInstruction: 1) Start the next story in the corrected sequence: wugs-s10 (branch-setup -> implementation-plan -> subagent-execution -> verify-completion -> branch-complete -> DoD, same full cycle as every prior story this session). CRITICAL: read wugs-s9's ACTUAL shipped code first (src/web-ui/routes/products.js's real handlePostApprovePromotion/handlePostRejectPromotion/_resolvePromotionRequest, now on merged master) before designing wugs-s10's implementation plan -- wugs-s10 is audit-logging for the request/approve/reject flow, so it needs the real shape of what it's logging, not the story/DoR text alone. 2) Continue watching for cross-story merge conflicts on shared functions in src/web-ui/routes/products.js -- wugs-s10/s11/s12 will very likely touch the same neighbourhood (module.exports, the require block, the promotion handlers) so a conflict is quite plausible if worktrees overlap; anticipate and hand-merge if it happens. 3) Process fix still in effect: proactively check E2E status (`gh pr checks <pr-number>`) immediately after every future branch-complete's `gh pr create` call, BEFORE reporting the branch-complete as done -- wugs-s9 stayed clean, but this is not proven structural, just circumstantial (see DoD Observation #2), so keep checking every time regardless. 4) New process fix from this story: when writing a DoD, verify BEFORE running gate-advance that the implementation plan artefact was actually committed somewhere during the task dispatches (git log --all --oneline -- <plan-path>) -- it's easy for a plan file written once at the start of implementation-plan to never get staged into any of the per-task commits, since each task's dispatch instructions only ever say to commit specific src/test files. 5) Also remember: `skills gate-advance` validates-then-applies-fields, it does NOT auto-populate `stage` -- always pass `stage=<gate-name>` explicitly as one of the field=value pairs, and check nested structures (like `tasks[]`) need a direct Edit + integrity-check pass afterward, not the advance CLI. 6) Also watch for the 'stuck subagent waiting on its own background process' failure mode discovered on wugs-s8 (Task 4) -- if a dispatched implementer's final report describes waiting for a background task to finish 'on its own', check the worktree's actual git status/diff/log directly rather than waiting for a report that will never come. 7) Process patterns proven effective all session, keep using them: full implementer -> spec-compliance -> code-quality -> fix -> re-review cycle for tasks with new logic (every one has surfaced a real finding across every story this session, including wugs-s9's CSRF gap); lighter single-dispatch-plus-self-verify for pure lock-in tasks (wugs-s9's Task 3 was pure lock-in, zero source changes needed, confirmed by dispatch report and spot-checked directly). Recompute and explicitly state expected test counts to dispatched agents when a plan's own per-task predictions have drifted due to review-added tests in earlier tasks -- wugs-s9's Task 4 dispatch correctly flagged this itself (plan said 6, actual was 10) rather than treating the mismatch as a failure. 8) For every pipeline-state.json write: fetch origin/master first and compare against HEAD before writing directly -- if no drift, safe to write directly; if there IS drift (as happened at wugs-s9's branch-complete step, because the worktree's feature branch was cut before the branch-setup bookkeeping commit landed on master), do the write from the main repo's master checkout, not the stale worktree copy. Baseline test count to expect: 33 pre-existing test-suite failures out of 515+ files, and 14 pre-existing pipeline-state-integrity failures -- confirm the FAILURE LIST matches the documented baseline (not just the count) before assuming any change is pre-existing.
